findings.description: The database username and password are rendered into EC2 user data and then written to a local PHP configuration file. User data is retrievable by processes on the instance and commonly accessible to principals allowed to describe the instance, broadening exposure of the database credential.

`publicly_accessible = true` assigns public connectivity capability to the RDS instance. Although the shown security-group ingress is limited to the VPC CIDR, exposing the database to public addressing increases its attack surface and makes future network-rule errors externally exploitable.

`storage_encrypted = false` leaves RDS database storage, automated backups, snapshots, and read replicas unencrypted at rest, exposing stored data if underlying storage or exported snapshots are accessed.

This rule permits all protocols and ports from the database security group to `0.0.0.0/0`. It provides an unrestricted outbound path that can enable data exfiltration or command-and-control traffic from a compromised database environment.

The EC2 instance role grants every S3, EC2, and RDS action against every resource. Compromise of the application instance or its instance credentials would allow broad account-wide data access and infrastructure modification, including likely privilege-escalation paths.
